summary: Both commands are one-shot operator actions, so throughput is irrelevant and the only real cost is how much of a client repo they read. That was the one genuine performance defect: the stale-reference report loaded whole files from the working tree. It now searches the git index, which streams blobs and skips ignored trees — the difference between bounded and unbounded on repos like the real target, which carries node_modules/ and dist/.

non_blocking_findings.summary: read_bytes() allocated every candidate file whole to search for a short marker, so a large tracked archive or generated bundle could exhaust memory — and it ran after the destructive steps, so the command would have failed only once the tree was already replaced.

The migrated-skills fallback rglob'd the freshly copied tree, descending into an ignored node_modules/ or dist/ inside a client skill despite the git ls-files bound, and re-reporting files already seen from Git.

residual_risks: The counterpart check still walks the legacy tree with rglob. That tree is vendored machinery — 65 files in the real target against the harness's 77 — so it is bounded by construction rather than by a guard.

stage migrate runs two git subprocesses to validate --base, and the symlink pass runs one cat-file per indexed symlink. Both are once-per-repo operator actions on sets that are normally empty or near-empty.
